notes:
Inbound via webinar and content marketing signup. Company: ProseHarbor — SMB SaaS that generates bulk marketing content (blogs, product descriptions, personalized email variants). Self-serve signups from marketing funnel; already claimed free credits and ran early volume tests.

Summary of needs:
- Primary: hosted_api (self-serve) with predictable unit economics for high-volume generation.
- Throughput: currently ~100k-150k tokens/day in tests; expecting growth to 500k+ tokens/day within 3 months if costs are acceptable.
- Latency: not strict single-request SLOs; they prefer batch/async throughput for nightly article generation, but use near-real-time for email personalization (~100-300ms acceptable for per-recipient).
- Cost sensitivity: HIGH. Repeated comment: "cost is the gating factor". Wants cost per 1k tokens comparisons and suggestions on batching/caching to reduce spend.
- Model preference: open/model variants that can be quantized; anything under $0.XX per 1k tokens equivalent. Interested in smaller quantized 7B/13B variants as fallback.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to cheaper model when quotas hit, or graceful degradation (shorter outputs).
- Caching/Binning: very interested in prefix caching for templated prompts and recommendations for batching windows (synchronous vs background jobs).
- Security: basic SOC2 attestation required; audit logging desirable. Public cloud only — no VPC/on-prem at this stage.

Quoted from discovery call: "We can’t justify the spend unless the token economics improve — show us realistic batching/caching wins." — Jonah Park.

Technical notes from Eng (Priya):
- Pipeline: templated prompt + per-customer variables; many repeated prefixes (good candidate for prefix cache).
- Current pain: per-request overhead and rate-limit throttling with their current vendor; looking for predictable webhook flows and token-level usage breakdowns.
- POC ask: small, time-boxed perf run showing cost/latency for 50k tokens/day and scaled to 500k with caching on/off.
